sources.title: Analyzing and Interpreting Data From Likert-Type Scales
sources.locator: Statements that responses on an ordinal scale can be ranked while the distance between responses is not measurable; that the differences between adjacent frequency responses are not necessarily equal; that the median suits ordered-category data alongside response frequencies; and that means and standard deviations belong to interval data where the difference between responses can be calculated.
sources.license: Open access under the journal's Creative Commons terms; facts-only use, with no source expression reused

uses.rightsBasisEvidence: Used only to verify facts about the ordinal status of ranked response categories, the absence of established equal spacing between adjacent categories, and which descriptive summaries suit ordered-category data as against interval data. No wording, table, figure, example, or item from the source was copied or adapted.
